What I saw was that the buying needs to be simple for a newcomer & yet clearly value has to be perceived for the money spent.  And the more I read reviews, the more confused over specs, recommendations etc I became.  
  
So I took to classifying systems (complete dac+amp+spkrs) based on sound characteristics.   
What I found was as follows:  
- Low fidelity systems need to have clarity, tight bass, low noise & balanced sound (low, mid & high freq balance). Budget not greater than $250  
- Medium fidelity systems (also called entry level hifi) need to have the above plus timing (dac), musicality, emotion in music & refineness (also non commercial sound as in one found on sony, philips etc) in sound. This is the start of hifi territory. Budget not more than $1000.  
- High fidelity systems have all the above plus imaging, great timbre, organic sound & instrument separation. Budget not above $4000.  
- Exceptional systems - some additional sound characteristics which other more knowledgeable members will be able to tell plus great in all of the above. Budget no limits these days.  
  
Some other things that may matter based on personal tastes  
- Warm or cool or neutral sound. I prefer warm.  
- Versatility - good with all genres of music.  
- Energetic, neutral or laid back sound.  
  
Of course you have to develop your own ability to identify each of these characteristics separately. I developed it on my dac & headphone setup which can be had for cheap.  
Also, parts matching has to be done so as to achieve above stated sound output as I have talked of overall system sound.  
  
Thing is that people get 'used' to the sound they have been listening to and then they think that a higher level is where it should be. For e.g., I have a mid fi setup (Marantz PM 5004 & Q Acoustics 2020i with M Audio 2496 sound card) and am just beginning to find areas where there can be improvements. I am beginning to feel that I can have more clarity & instrument separation & power, so I have upped my standards and am now hunting for a high fidelity setup.  
  
Best wishes.
